Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Sube Shrine'''|須倍神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|ckb|پارێزگای تۆتۆمی|cs|Tótómi (provincie)|de|Provinz Tōtōmi|eo|Provinco Totomi|es|Provincia de Tōtōmi|fa|ولایت توتومی|fr|Province de Tōtōmi|gl|Provincia de Tōtōmi|id|Provinsi Tōtōmi|it|Tōtōmi|ja|遠江国|ko|도토미국|lt|Totomio žemė|nl|Totomi (provincie)|pt|Província de Tōtōmi|ru|Тотоми (провинция)|simple|Tōtōmi Province|sk|Tótómi|sr|Провинција Тотоми|tr|Tōtōmi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тотомі|zh|遠江國|zh_min_nan|Tôtômi-kok|zh_yue|遠江國|qid=Q1048864|lt=Tōtōmi Province}}.

== Overview ==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in {{ill|Ninna|de|Ninna|fa|نیننا|fr|Ère Ninna|hr|Ninna|ia|Ninna|id|Ninna|ja|仁和|ko|닌나|ru|Нинна (нэнго)|sh|Ninna|simple|Ninna|sr|Нина (ера)|th|นินนะ|tr|Ninna|uk|Нінна (ненґо)|zh|仁和 (日本)|zh_yue|仁和 (年號)|qid=Q1346317}} 3 (887), during the reign of the 58th emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōkō|ar|الإمبراطور كوكو|arz|كوكو (شاعر من اليابان)|azb|کوکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Koko|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆکۆ|cs|Kókó|de|Kōkō|el|Αυτοκράτορας Κόκο|es|Kōkō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوکو|fr|Kōkō|id|Kaisar Kōkō|it|Kōkō|ja|光孝天皇|ko|고코 천황|ms|Maharaja Kōkō|nl|Koko (keizer)|pl|Kōkō|pt|Koko (imperador)|ru|Император Коко|sh|Car Kōkō|sl|Cesar Kōkō|sv|Koko (kejsare)|sw|Koko wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิโคโก|tl|Emperador Kōkō|tr|Kōkō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Коко|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōkō|yo|Emperor Kōkō|zh|光孝天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôkô Thian-hông|qid=Q440518}}. Its location, {{ill|Miyakodacho|ja|都田町|qid=Q131901548}}, developed as a {{ill|mikuriya|ja|御厨|qid=Q11488831}} of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168}}, and the deities are thought to have been invited from Ise. Originally, the Inner Shrine stood as upper shrine on Uenoyama in Kami-Miyakoda Sube, and the Outer Shrine stood as lower shrine in Nakatsu of Shimo-Miyakoda. In {{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} 2 (902), both were moved to the present site and came to be called {{ill|Shinmei shrines|ja|神明神社|simple|Shinmei shrines|zh|神明神社|qid=Q11590310|lt=Shinmei-gū}} or Sube Shrine.

== Festivals ==
At the autumn {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=annual grand festival}}, floats from nine surrounding districts (Kawayama, Araki, Yokoo, Yoshikage, Tanigami, Isshiki, Nakatsu, Nakano, Sube) are pulled around. Also, at the {{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭|simple|Kinensai|th|คิเน็นไซ|qid=Q118906710}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|de|Niiname-sai|fr|Niiname-no-Matsuri|id|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|ko|신상제 (11월)|simple|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518}}, children selected from duty districts and ujiko participate by serving offering rites and dedicating {{ill|Urayasu no mai|ja|浦安の舞|qid=Q11558194}} (sword dance and bell dance).
